questions.question: What is media imperialism?
options: The theory that dominant nations exert disproportionate influence over global media flows
The use of drones in journalism
questions.explanation: Media imperialism describes the one-way flow of news and culture from powerful, mainly English-speaking Western nations to the rest of the world.

questions.question: When was the BBC World Service founded?
questions.explanation: The BBC World Service began in 1932 as the BBC Empire Service and now reaches hundreds of millions of people weekly in over 40 languages.

questions.question: What is "gatekeeping" in the media?
options: The process by which information is filtered and selected before reaching audiences
questions.explanation: Gatekeeping is the filtering of information; when English dominates international news, it shapes which stories and perspectives reach global audiences.

questions.question: What is the "CNN effect"?
options: The idea that 24-hour global news coverage can influence government policy and public responses
A technical fault in cable TV
questions.explanation: The CNN effect refers to how round-the-clock global news coverage can pressure policymakers and shape international responses to crises.

questions.question: Why does English's dominance in global news matter?
options: It determines whose voices and perspectives shape international understanding of events
questions.explanation: Because major global news agencies operate in English, anglophone framings and priorities disproportionately shape how the world understands events.
